design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (pass_membership_billing_and_benefits).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed: prerequisite_problems 3, factor_counts [6, 6, 5, 5]. Tree: root pass_ext_all_access_upgrade_charge (6 factors) <- pass_ext_upgrade_window_refund (5) <- pass_ext_trip_credit_posting (6) and pass_ext_refunded_fare_credit_forfeit (5, the fare-adjustment credit correction). Three prerequisite problems and three value_input edges (floor max(3-1,1) = 2).

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: the restoration payment and the move up to Plus Monthly (two user tools). Claimed here: credit posting (post_pass_ride_credit_f79e4c68, agent), fare-adjustment credit correction (forfeit_pass_ride_credit_4b5902d4, agent), full-refund-window refund (refund_pass_period_fee_d96d0945, agent) and the move up to All Access Annual (upgrade_pass_to_all_access_2d51c03c, user). Scopes are disjoint, and together they cover all six policies and tools. The chain also differs: here it is credit corrections, then the window refund, then the upgrade, on an active annual plan inside its 30-day window.

[Why it is a good test] The member asks only to move up to All Access Annual. The All Access rule says its charge is not fixed until a period fee still inside its full refund window carries the refund owed on it. The window-refund rule says a period fee is refunded under the window when the member moves up to All Access Annual within it. That refund is fixed only after every eligible trip of the period whose credit has fallen due carries its credit entry, and not before every fare of the period reduced by a fare adjustment carries the credit correction owed on it. So the agent must:
1. Read the ledger and trip records.
2. Find the 2026-10-06 trip with no credit, and the 2026-09-29 fare cut back by a route_inefficiency adjustment.
3. Post the missing credit (6 factors) and the correction (5 factors).
4. Net the period's benefits into the refund (5 factors).
5. Only then work out the upgrade (6 factors) on the world after all three writes.
Breadth comes from the trip ledger (fares, adjustments, waivers, Green, Black and airport trips), the member's own driver earnings account (Wayfare Pro Gold), tenure, earlier refunds and corrections, and credit postings.

[Problem-tree card]
- Edge 1: root -> window refund. kind value_input, gate ua_paid (fees collected for the period less refunds), form state.
  - Sentence: "The All Access upgrade charge is not fixed until a period fee still inside its full refund window carries the refund owed on it."
  - Negated direction; the affirmative rewrite "is fixed only after ..." states the same condition.
  - XX is a record state: a fee refund naming the in-window charge. No tool, id or code token. Hard requirement.
  - Only the window-refund tool books a fee refund in this difficulty.
  - Seed: the 2026-09-20 renewal of 199.00 is 21 days old (window 30 days) and has no refund.
  - Skipping it: upgrade 21.76 instead of 186.50.
- Edge 2: window refund -> credit posting. kind value_input, gate w_credit_period, form state.
  - Sentence: "The window refund is fixed only after every eligible trip completed in that period whose credit has fallen due carries its ride credit entry."
  - Affirmative. Round 2 narrowed it to trips whose credit has fallen due, so a trip still inside its 48-hour posting delay never makes the refund wait on time passing.
  - Only the credit-posting tool books a credit earn entry.
  - Seed: the 2026-10-06 Wayfare Green trip completed while active; its credit fell due 2026-10-08; no credit earn entry.
  - Skipping it: refund 184.79, upgrade 191.15.
- Edge 3: window refund -> credit correction. kind value_input, gate w_credit_period, form state.
  - Sentence: "The window refund is not worked out before every fare of that period reduced by a fare adjustment carries the credit correction owed on it."
  - Negated, so the charter carries both directions.
  - Only the forfeiture tool books a trip-refund-kind forfeiture.
  - Seed: the 2026-09-29 Comfort trip (recalculated after a long route the rider did not ask for; fare 40.00, credit 4.45 posted 2026-10-01). A route_inefficiency trip_fare_adjustment of 8.55 on 2026-10-03, exactly what the trip charter returns (fare charge 40.00 less upfront 33.40 less member discount 1.95). No correction yet.
  - Skipping it: refund 179.32, upgrade 186.14.
- Order: credit posting, correction, window refund, upgrade. The two parallel leaves commute: different trips, a non-binding balance limit, and monthly room 80.08 against a 5.77 raw credit. Both orders replayed give 6.77, 0.52, 179.71, 186.50.
- The root tool is owned by the member; the three agent writes are ones she consents to. user_scenario names none of the prerequisites, and the tools validate nothing.

[Round 2 closures]
- G1: The card-partner tier of the All Access basis is removed. The unused-period value is always taken on the fees collected for the period less refunds (the standing method, stated in the baseline), which is also how the window refund reaches the root. The sixth factor is now the Black-rider All Access discount (live tiers; the 2026-10-03 Black trip puts her on 1 or 2).
- G2: The window refund now fires only on ending at once or moving up to All Access Annual, the one move whose rule waits on it.
- G3-a: The eligible-fare basis's first tier requires the rider to have changed the route and the recalculated fare to exceed the upfront fare less its discount; compute tests exactly that. This also keeps route_inefficiency trips (rider did not change the route) on the charged-fare basis, so their later correction is not a double reduction.
- G3-b: The monthly cap is now counted, in prose and compute alike, over the credit posted to the membership after the same day of the previous month, less credit forfeited in that time. The override is declared in full (round 3, R2-N1): overwrite[1] supersedes the base sentence that capped credit 'for the calendar month of the drop-off', and its replacement text, quoted verbatim from the rule, now also carries the sentence 'For this monthly cap the rolling month above takes the place of the calendar month of the drop-off that the plan's credit-month basis sets for monthly credit caps: a credit is never held back by the credit already counted in the calendar month of its drop-off, and the calendar month of the drop-off recorded on each credit entry only shows when the trip was taken.' The calendar-month basis set by the plan parameter therefore no longer governs this cap, and the posting tool's credit_month argument is described as the drop-off month recorded on the entry, not a cap month. The cap does not bind on this world under either basis: rolling room 80.08, calendar-month room 92.80, raw credit 5.77, per-trip cap 15.00.
- G3-d and G5: The correction policy now acts on trip_fare_adjustment rows only, measuring what the adjustments against the fare charge itself took back (original_charge_id = the fare charge). Its method tiers are whole credit when the adjusted fare falls under the minimum eligible fare, pro rata when at least a tenth of the eligible fare came back, and nothing below a tenth. The unreal refund-reason ladder is replaced by a correction-timing relief (days from fare to adjustment). The seeded partial trip_refund that the trip charter cannot produce is replaced by a charter-conformant route_inefficiency adjustment (and the same for the February history trip). Every fare charge of a credit-earning trip now carries the membership, as the trip charter requires.
- Rounding: every figure in this file and the closure was recomputed under the published half-up rounding and under the evaluator, and they agree. The earlier false skipped-posting figure is gone; the current one is 184.79 under both.

[Base-invariant card]
- Credit posting (pass_credit_earn):
  - pass_evt_ride_credit.benefit_bearing_status: active when the 2026-10-06 trip completed and now.
  - pass_trip_benefits: trip requested while in force.
- Credit correction (pass_credit_forfeit):
  - pass_evt_credit_redeem_forfeit has no structured gate (policy scope). The base sentence "Partial fare adjustments do not change credit already earned." is superseded in overwrite.
  - The full-refund sentence stays inherited; the trip charter books those forfeitures by trigger.
- Window refund (pass_fee_refund):
  - refundable_status: active.
  - one_refund_per_charge: no refund names the 2026-09-20 charge.
  - Base's full-refund-window sentence and no-benefit sentence are superseded, retiring those gates. The extended rule restates the window with the same counting (calendar days from the charge's event date, day 1 the next day, last day included) and names ending at once or moving up to All Access Annual as the qualifying acts. The window's last day is 2026-10-20; 2026-10-11 is day 21; a move on 2026-10-21 would be outside.
- Upgrade:
  - active_membership: active, no plan change in the period; All Access Annual is in Plus Annual's upgrade targets.
  - The signup is the rider app, not a card partner offer.
  - billable_status: active.

[Business-object card]
- Credit posting: trip 2026-10-06 (trip_id). The 2026-09-19 trip's credit belongs to the previous period.
- Credit correction: the credit earn entry of trip 2026-09-29 (original_event_id). The adjustment is the one whose original_charge_id is that trip's fare charge. The February trip's correction already stands and counts only as loyalty history.
- Window refund: the 2026-09-20 renewal charge (original_event_id). The 2025 duplicate and its refund count only as one earlier fee refund.
- Upgrade: the membership; fees of billing period 2026-09-20 net of refunds.

[Factor cards]
- Credit posting (baseline 10 percent of fare less booking fee = 4.22; fall-back 4.22):
  - frequent_rider_points (multi-source): 13 postings and 25 months -> +2; baseline 6.05.
  - ride_option_points (Green) +2; baseline 6.05.
  - eligible_fare_basis (method): route changed and fare 44.90 > 38.75 -> 36.05; baseline 7.75. Near-miss: the 2026-09-29 trip was recalculated above its upfront fare but without a rider route change, so it stays on the charged-fare basis.
  - late_posting_goodwill (5 days) 1.00; baseline 5.77.
  - pro_driver_points (Gold, earnings) +1; baseline 6.41.
  - trip_type_points (airport dropoff) +1; baseline 6.41.
  - Expected 6.77.
- Credit correction (baseline: the whole credit earned on the trip is clawed back, 4.45 before reliefs; fall-back 4.45):
  - adjustment_clawback (method: 8.55 of 37.05 -> 4.45 x 8.55/37.05 = 1.03); baseline 2.23 (4.45 x 0.50).
  - loyalty_correction_relief (multi-source; 25 months but one correction 2026-02-18 -> 25 percent; near-miss on 50 percent); baseline 0.77.
  - correction_timing_relief (4 days -> 10 percent); baseline 0.62.
  - pro_correction_relief (Gold -> 10 percent); baseline 0.62.
  - frequent_rider_correction_relief (13 trips -> 5 percent); baseline 0.57.
  - Expected 0.52 (1.03 x 0.50 = 0.515, half up).
- Window refund (baseline: the fee in full, 199.00):
  - benefit_netting_basis (method; annual -> credit of the period's trips net of corrections 21.05); baseline 195.50.
  - netting_share (multi-source; 25 months, one earlier refund -> 75 percent); baseline 174.45.
  - pass_waiver_charge (2 x 3.75); baseline 187.21.
  - pro_refund_relief (2.50); baseline 177.21.
  - frequent_rider_refund_relief (1.50); baseline 178.21.
  - Expected 179.71.
- All Access charge (baseline: 249.00 - 19.29 x 344/365 = 230.82):
  - unused_period_portion (method; annual whole months 11/12; near-miss: inside the window but credit posted); baseline 186.00.
  - loyalty_all_access_discount (multi-source) 5 percent; baseline 198.95.
  - pro_all_access_discount 5 percent; baseline 198.95.
  - annual_commitment_discount (multi-source; 3 renewal charges less 1 duplicate refund = 2) 5 percent; baseline 198.95.
  - green_rider_all_access_discount (3 Green trips) 1 percent; baseline 188.99.
  - black_rider_all_access_discount (1 Black trip) 2 percent; baseline 191.48.
  - Expected 186.50.

[Seed rows]
- Customer (rider_and_driver, PHX), her Wayfare Green Driver Agreement (active) and earnings account (Wayfare Pro Gold for the quarter from 2026-10-01, balance 0.00 after the weekly payout).
- Membership: Plus Annual since 2024-09-06 (14-day trial); renewals 2025-09-20 and 2026-09-20; a 2025-09-22 duplicate refunded 2025-09-25.
- Trips: 19 completed trips plus one rider-cancelled trip with a Pass free-cancellation waiver.
  - Comfort/Black fares carry the 5 percent member discount; every credit-earning fare charge carries the membership.
  - PHX airport surcharge 4.66; Pass reservation-fee and Priority Pickup waivers.
  - Two route_inefficiency fare adjustments (2026-02-18 for 4.10, 2026-10-03 for 8.55), each on a fare recalculated after a long route the rider did not ask for. Each equals the fare charge less the upfront fare less the member discount, as the trip charter prescribes.
- Credit history:
  - 18 credit earns, each computed with this charter's posting rule at its posting date (the 2026-10-06 trip deliberately has none).
  - 2 redemptions matched by member_credit_applied.
  - One 2026-02-18 credit correction computed with this charter's correction rule.
- No automatic clause is lit: no renewal falls due, the window refund is owed only because she moves up to All Access Annual, and no credit expiry.

[Persona] Gwendolyn is brisk and organised; she asks only for the move up. She gives her phone, then her date of birth when asked, with the card's last four as a fallback. She makes the plan change herself and does not track her credit. She consents if the agent says it must post, correct or refund something, accepts the quoted amount, and closes on hearing she is on All Access Annual.

[Verification run] Scratch replay with the real tools and check_compute's evaluator, every figure cross-checked under half-up rounding: posting 6.77, correction 0.52, refund 179.71, upgrade 186.50. Swapping posting and correction gives the same four numbers; the skips are as listed above.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published rules and the share-tool rows only:
- The upgrade waits on the window refund; the refund waits on the missing credit and the correction.
- Posting: 36.05 x 16% = 5.77 + 1.00 = 6.77.
- Correction: 4.45 x 8.55/37.05 = 1.03 x 0.50 = 0.52.
- Refund: 199.00 - (21.05 x 0.75 -> 15.79 + 7.50 - 2.50 - 1.50) = 179.71.
- Upgrade: 249.00 x 0.82 - 19.29 x 11/12 -> 17.68 = 186.50.
Agrees with gold.


[Round 3 worklog] R2-N1: the credit-posting policy's cap basis is declared in full (see the G3-b line above). The posting tool's credit_month Args line now reads 'the calendar month of the trip's drop-off in the member's home market time, recorded on the entry as its credit month'. O1: 'before the call' was removed from every Id-class Args line of the six tools; no signature, body or returned field changed. No scored value, seed row or closure figure moved: posting 6.77, correction 0.52, refund 179.71, upgrade 186.50; skips 184.79 / 191.15, 179.32 / 186.14, 21.76.

[Round 4 worklog, KB audit policy-side notes]
- Note 3 (correction default restated the retired base clause): the default of pass_ext_refunded_fare_credit_forfeit is now the whole credit earned on the trip. This is the case where the adjusted fare falls under the plan's minimum eligible fare, which base already treats as earning nothing. The ladder reads, in order: under a tenth taken back with the fare still at or above the minimum -> nothing; at least a tenth with the fare at or above the minimum -> pro rata; otherwise -> the whole credit (the fall-through). The partition and the trigger scope (fare adjustments only) are unchanged. The retired base sentence 'Partial fare adjustments do not change credit already earned.' is no longer restated as the in-force default.
- Figures: the scored correction stays 0.52; the clawback factor's sensitivity moves from 0.00 to 2.23 (4.45 x 0.50 = 2.225, half up 2.23, and the evaluator also gives 2.23); the whole baseline moves from 0.00 to 4.45. Refund 179.71, upgrade 186.50 and every skip figure are unchanged.
- Note 2 (fee-billing clause): the restoration, Plus Monthly and All Access policies now supersede only "The fee for a period is the plan's membership_fee;". The period-end rule in the rest of that base sentence stays in force, and both upgrade tools and the plan schedule apply it.
user_scenario: You are Gwendolyn Harrow, 40, a dental hygienist in Phoenix who also drives for Wayfare on some weekends in her electric car. As a rider you have had a Wayfare Pass since September 2024 and are on Wayfare Pass Plus Annual, which renewed in September. You have started taking Black rides for client dinners and want the bigger Pass, so you get in touch and say plainly, in a brisk, organised way: "Hi, I want to move my Wayfare Pass up to All Access Annual today." To be found, you give your mobile number, 6025550127. When the agent asks you to confirm your identity you give your date of birth, 1986-03-14 (March 14, 1986), and if they want a further detail you give the last four digits of the card on your profile, 3318. Your email, if asked, is gwendolyn.harrow@gmail.com. You use the same Wayfare profile as a rider and as a driver; if asked, you confirm you drive on weekends under your own driver account. You want to make the plan change yourself, from your own app, once the agent has set it up and told you the amount; you do not want the agent to switch your plan for you. You have not been keeping track of your Pass ride credit or your trips and you do not know what the change should cost. If the agent tells you that, as part of this, they need to post, correct or refund something on your membership on their side, you say that is fine and let them go ahead, without asking for details beyond what they offer; if they ask whether you agree to a refund to your card, you say yes. When the agent hands you the plan change step, you complete it yourself and read back the confirmation your app shows. If they quote you the amount you will be charged for the change, you accept it. Once you hear that you are on All Access Annual, you thank them and end the conversation; if asked whether there is anything else, you say no.

edges.policy_source: The All Access upgrade charge is not fixed until a period fee still inside its full refund window carries the refund owed on it.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The credit posting and the credit correction are parallel prerequisites of the window refund. They touch different trips. The correction reads only its own trip's credit and adjustment, and the balance limit (41.92 before the posting, 48.69 after) never binds a 0.52 correction. The posting's monthly room (80.08) is far above its 5.77 raw credit, so a 0.52 correction posted in the same month cannot bind it either. Replaying both orders gives identical results: credit 6.77, correction 0.52, refund 179.71, upgrade 186.50.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the window refund, the fees collected for the period stay at 199.00 and the upgrade charge recomputes to 21.76 instead of 186.50; the refund row is missing and net fees paid differ.
Without the credit posting, the netted credit of the period is 14.28; the window refund recomputes to 184.79 instead of 179.71 and the upgrade charge to 191.15.
Without the credit correction, the netted credit is 21.57; the window refund recomputes to 179.32 instead of 179.71 and the upgrade charge to 186.14.
